title.rendered: The Sacrifice of Praise: The Fruit of Our Lips | The Thankful Heart, Day 8

excerpt.rendered: Hebrews 13:15 calls us to continually offer the sacrifice of praise, the fruit of our lips. Day 8 of The Thankful Heart offers praise through Him.

content.rendered:
Under the old covenant, worshippers brought lambs and bulls to the altar. Under the new covenant, the final sacrifice has already been made. What we bring now is the fruit of our lips: thanks offered through Jesus, continually.

The Gospel For Today | Sunday, November 22, 2026 | The Thankful Heart, Day 8

Today’s Scripture

“Therefore by Him let us continually offer the sacrifice of praise to God, that is, the fruit of our lips, giving thanks to His name. But do not forget to do good and to share, for with such sacrifices God is well pleased.”
Hebrews 13:15-16 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

The letter to the Hebrews spends chapter after chapter showing that Jesus is the better High Priest and the once-for-all sacrifice. The blood of bulls and goats could never take away sins, but Christ offered one sacrifice for sins forever and sat down at the right hand of God (Hebrews 10:12). The altar is finished. The work is done. So when the writer reaches the end of the letter, the question naturally comes: what offering is left for us to bring?

The answer is in verse 15. “Therefore by Him let us continually offer the sacrifice of praise to God.” Notice the first two words: by Him. We do not offer praise to make up for anything. We offer it through Jesus, because of Jesus, standing in what He has already finished. Our praise is not a payment. It is a thank-you note written in response to a gift.

Why is it called a sacrifice? Because sometimes it costs us. It is easy to praise when the house is full and the bills are paid. It is a sacrifice to praise in the hospital car park, after the redundancy letter, in a hard week in Manila or a lonely season in Dubai. Praise that rises when we do not feel like it is precious to God, not because He needs it, but because it declares that He is still good when everything else says otherwise.

The writer then defines it: “the fruit of our lips, giving thanks to His name.” Praise is spoken. It comes out of our mouths. And it is continual: not just on Sunday, but on Monday and Thursday too. Then verse 16 adds the other side: “do not forget to do good and to share.” Thanksgiving with our lips overflows into generosity with our hands. A thankful heart becomes an open hand.

Today is the Lord’s Day. Wherever you gather, whether a cathedral in London or a small fellowship in a Lagos living room, bring the sacrifice that pleases Him. Sing it, say it, pray it. Then go and share something with someone. The altar has been settled by Jesus. Our part is to keep the praise flowing through Him.

How the Thankful Heart Worships

It praises through Jesus, not to earn. The sacrifice for sin is finished; our praise is a response, not a payment.

It praises when it costs. Thanks offered in a hard place is a true sacrifice of praise.

It overflows into sharing. The fruit of our lips leads to good done with our hands.

Declaration

Lord Jesus, I thank You that You offered one sacrifice for sins forever and sat down at the right hand of God (Hebrews 10:12). Nothing is left for me to pay. By You I continually offer the sacrifice of praise to God, the fruit of my lips, giving thanks to Your name (Hebrews 13:15). When praise costs me something, I still lift it, because You are good. I thank You for all You have given me, and I share it freely with others. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
